days.topic: Topic 19: Lipids · Types by Structure and Membrane Lipids
clues: A derived lipid: no fatty acids, only three six-membered rings and one five-membered ring fused together.
It sits in the cell membrane, where it regulates how fluid the membrane is.
HDL carries the good kind and LDL the bad kind through the blood.
days.why: Cholesterol is a steroid, so it is a derived lipid built on the fused steroid nucleus. It is a membrane lipid that regulates fluidity, and lipoproteins (HDL, LDL) transport it in the blood.

days.topic: Topic 18: Enzymes · Structure: Cofactors and Key Terms
clues: A non-protein helper that is bound and released easily, held only by intermolecular forces.
It is organic and is often derived from a vitamin.
CoA and NADH are examples; it is the loosely bound type of cofactor.
days.why: A coenzyme is a cofactor that is loosely bound (intermolecular forces only), organic and often vitamin-derived, like CoA and NADH. The tightly bound kind is a prosthetic group.

days.topic: Topic 17: Proteins and Optical Isomerism · Secondary, Tertiary and Quaternary Structure
clues: A multimeric protein with quaternary structure: a tetramer whose subunits are held by noncovalent forces.
Two α chains of 141 residues and two β chains of 146 residues.
Each chain has a heme with iron, so it carries four O₂ from the lungs to the tissues.
days.why: Hemoglobin is the tetramer α₂β₂, so it has quaternary structure, and each chain's heme iron binds one O₂. Myoglobin has one chain and one heme, stores O₂ in muscle and has no quaternary structure.

days.topic: Lesson 8: GI Drugs · H2 Blockers and PPIs
clues: It keeps histamine off a receptor on the parietal cell, and it is the prototype of its group.
The least potent of its group, at 800 mg.
Its known adverse effect is gynecomastia; spironolactone is the other drug that does this.
days.why: Cimetidine is the prototype H2 blocker. It is the least potent of the four (800 mg; famotidine is the most potent) and causes gynecomastia through CYP450 and estrogen metabolism.

clues: A stimulant: it directly irritates the GI lining, and it belongs to the anthraquinones.
It is sold as a tea that some people misuse to lose weight.
Chronic users get melanosis coli: dark, giraffe-like spots in the colon.
days.why: Senna is the important anthraquinone stimulant laxative. Long-term use causes melanosis coli, and it is sold as Biofitea and Senokot Forte.
